steps.label: The chemical name
lines: The chemical name of plaster of
It is made by heating the mineral
steps.why: Plaster of Paris is a common name. The chemical name states the compound and how much water of crystallisation it holds: calcium sulphate carrying half a water molecule for each formula unit.
common_mistakes: Writing calcium sulphate dihydrate. That is gypsum, the material plaster of Paris is made from.
Writing calcium carbonate or calcium sulphite. The compound is a sulphate.
steps.memory_tip: Hemi means half, so hemihydrate means half a water molecule for each calcium sulphate unit.
steps.margin_note: Write the full name. Calcium sulphate on its own leaves out the water.

steps.why: The half water molecule is the point of the formula. Doubling everything clears the fraction, which is why the same compound is written in two ways and both are correct.
common_mistakes: Writing CaSO₄·2H₂O. That formula is gypsum, which holds two water molecules.
Dropping the water and writing CaSO₄ only. That is the anhydrous salt.
steps.memory_tip: Gypsum holds two water molecules, plaster of Paris only half of one.
steps.margin_note: Either CaSO₄·½H₂O or 2CaSO₄·H₂O is a correct form.

insider_note: This question asks for two exact items, the chemical name and the formula, so write both and keep the rest of the answer short.
